claims.text: Enhancing chemical short-range order together with grain refinement increases the hardness and strength of a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Chemical short-range order creates local energy barriers through diffuse antiphase boundaries.
Increasing grain-boundary density creates obstacles that impede dislocation motion.
An equiatomic MoNbTaW or AlCoCrFeNi alloy can provide a random-solid-solution baseline.
The baseline alloy has relatively coarse grains, exemplified by a grain size greater than 50 micrometers.
A controlled sub-solvus heat treatment can induce pronounced short-range order.
The proposed processing route can simultaneously refine grains without producing secondary phases.
The controlled comparison should use identical overall chemistries while varying short-range order and grain size.
Local chemically ordered regions produce diffuse antiphase boundaries along slip planes.
Enhanced short-range order raises the energy cost of dislocation glide because dislocations must disrupt local chemical order.
Grain refinement reduces the dislocation mean free path.
Short-range order and grain refinement act synergistically to increase hardness and yield strength relative to a random, coarse-grained solid solution.
The processed alloy will show a hardness increase of approximately 15% or more.
The processed alloy will have higher yield strength than the baseline.
The strengthening effect is limited to temperatures below those at which high-temperature softening eliminates the effect of short-range order.
The hypothesis applies only when the treatment does not form detrimental secondary phases.
The individual quantitative contributions of short-range order and grain-boundary strengthening, and their dependence on composition and processing, are uncertain.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant hardness and yield-strength increase after confirmed induction of short-range order and grain refinement would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to confirm short-range order and reduced grain size would itself falsify the hypothesis.
